claim: This is wrong or unsupported: The finding says the draft overstates the legal force by implying parties are required to aim for the temperature goal. But the draft itself says the temperature goal is a collective global objective and that the Agreement's language is 'aims at,' not a Party-level obligation. The objection is therefore not supported by the notes.
passage: This is the Agreement’s **collective global objective**, not a separate binding country-level temperature cap.

claim: This is wrong or unsupported: The notes do not show the sustainable-development/poverty wording, so the draft’s attribution of that extra language is unsupported.
passage: Holding the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels...

claim: Article 4(3) says each successive NDC will represent a progression beyond the Party's then current NDC and reflect its highest possible ambition, in light of common but differentiated responsibilities and national circumstances. The gloss of progression as movement in scope, coverage or implementation is not source text and is dropped.
passage: Each Party’s successive nationally determined contribution will represent a progression beyond the Party’s then current nationally determined contribution and reflect its highest possible ambition

claim: Article 14(1) says the stocktake assesses collective progress towards the Agreement's purpose and long-term goals. The claim that it does not assign responsibility to specific countries is the report's inference from this collective framing and should not be attributed to a quoted UNFCCC explainer passage.
passage: to assess the collective progress towards achieving the purpose of this Agreement and its long-term goals

claim: Article 4(9) requires NDC communication every five years, informed by the outcomes of the global stocktake. Article 14(2) sets the first stocktake in 2023 and every five years thereafter. The claim of deliberate, precise timing alignment is interpretive and is not supported by the notes.
passage: Each Party shall communicate a nationally determined contribution every five years ... and be informed by the outcomes of the global stocktake referred to in Article 14.

claim: This is wrong or unsupported: 'Ratchet' appears only as the draft’s label; it is not language from the notes or the treaty text quoted there.
passage: Each Party’s successive nationally determined contribution will represent a progression beyond the Party’s then current nationally determined contribution

claim: Article 2(1)(a) states a collective global temperature goal (well below 2°C, pursuing efforts toward 1.5°C). It is not a Party-level legal requirement or a separate country-level cap, so the wording that Parties are required to aim for it should be dropped.
passage: This is the Agreement’s **collective global objective**, not a separate binding country-level temperature cap.

claim: Article 4(2) says each Party shall prepare, communicate and maintain successive NDCs that it intends to achieve and shall pursue domestic mitigation measures aiming to achieve their objectives. The labels real policy commitments and intentionally decentralized architecture are not supported by the notes and are dropped.
passage: Each Party shall prepare, communicate and maintain successive nationally determined contributions that it intends to achieve.

claim: The notes support only that the UNFCCC NDC page describes NDCs as at the heart of the Agreement and says each Party must prepare, communicate and maintain successive NDCs. The responsibility-of-Parties phrasing and the emphasis on successive nature should not be attributed to that page.
passage: NDCs are at the heart of the Agreement
